newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Rosneft oil firm privatisation approved.
newsitem.headline: Russian Rosneft oil firm privatisation approved.

text.p: Russia's State Property Committee has approved a plan to privatise state oil holding firm Rosneft, committee spokeswoman Larisa Chernyshova said on Thursday.

Interfax News Agency said 51 percent of Rosneft shares would remain government property for three years, two percent would be given to workers and the remaining 48 percent would be offered through tenders and auctions.
Rosneft's crude oil output rose in 1996 to 13.1 million tonnes from 12.8 million tonnes in 1995, according to preliminary data.
A senior Rosneft official said earlier this week that the company planned to attract capital by issuing financial instruments, possibly Eurobonds.

Rosneft's privatisation has been delayed over quarrels with competitor SIDANKO (Sibirsko-Dalnevostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya) over ownership of prize crude oil producer Purneftegaz, which now belongs to Rosneft.

Rosneft was created out of the Rosneft state enterprise in 1995. It is the state's agents in all oil production-sharing deals, but saw many of its assets apportioned to newly-created vertically-integrated oil companies in recent years.
